ideas.pitch: Real-time driver HUD and telemetry system for wireless rovers using ESP32 and WebSockets to optimize lap times.
ideas.problem_statement: Overdrive is a high-speed wireless rover racing challenge on a Melbourne F1-style track featuring ramps, rollers, gravel pits, and airborne sections.
ideas.title: AeroDrive Telemetry & HUD
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on the live demo and hardware-software integration pattern seen in winning hardware hacks, giving the single operator crucial real-time sensor feedback to shave seconds off the final time.

ideas.pitch: Precision lap and checkpoint counting module utilizing a front-mounted white LED and LDR sensor configuration with onboard logging.
ideas.problem_statement: Checkpoint detection will be performed using a front-mounted white LED and LDR-based checkpoint system to calculate Final Time = Race Time + Penalty Time.
ideas.title: CheckpointPasser LDR Counter
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the exact penalty and checkpoint calculation method specified in the event flow, ensuring strict compliance and zero missed checkpoints.

ideas.pitch: Custom 3D-printed chassis and modular dampening system designed to absorb impact from ramps and airborne sections while keeping total weight under the 2 kg limit.
ideas.problem_statement: Teams compete to complete a Melbourne F1-style track featuring ramps, rollers, gravel pits, and airborne sections within a maximum weight of 2 kg and 8x8x8 inches dimensions.
ideas.title: RoverGrip Suspension & Weight Optimizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the unusual physical build pattern by directly solving the strict dimension and weight constraints required to survive high-impact jumps.

ideas.pitch: Optimized ESP-NOW or nRF24L01 wireless controller firmware reducing command latency to sub-10ms for hairpin turns and high-speed straights.
ideas.problem_statement: Control: Wireless only — Wi-Fi, BLE, RF, LoRa, nRF24L01, or commercial RC systems with a single operator per run.
ideas.title: LowLatency RC Control Bridge
ideas.why_it_could_win: Executes on robust hardware-level wireless communication which directly dictates success in high-speed racing challenges where lag causes crashes.

ideas.pitch: Safe power distribution and voltage monitoring circuit keeping the max 48V DC supply stable across sudden motor surges during rapid acceleration.
ideas.problem_statement: Pre-requisites: Competition-ready wireless-controlled rover complying with specifications including a maximum voltage of 48V DC.
ideas.title: PowerGuard 48V Voltage Reg
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the pattern of robust, reliable hardware engineering and safety compliance seen in winning C/C++ hardware and IoT projects.
